questions.text: The recurrence relation that arises in relation with the complexity of binary search is:
questions.solution:
Binary search does a constant amount of work (one comparison) and then searches one half: [latex]T(n)=T(n/2)+k[/latex], which gives [latex]O(\log n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]T(n)=T(n/2)+k[/latex]

questions.text:
A message is made up entirely of characters from the set X= {P,Q,R,S,T}. The table of probabilities for each of the characters is shown below:

If a message of 100 characters over X is encoded using Huffman coding, then the expected length of the encoded message in bits is_____
questions.solution:
Huffman: T (0.08) + R (0.17) = 0.25; S (0.19) + P (0.22) = 0.41; 0.25 + Q (0.34) = 0.59; 0.41 + 0.59.
Code lengths: Q 2, S 2, P 2, T 3, R 3.

Average = 0.34[latex]\cdot[/latex]2 + 0.19[latex]\cdot[/latex]2 + 0.22[latex]\cdot[/latex]2 + 0.08[latex]\cdot[/latex]3 + 0.17[latex]\cdot[/latex]3 = 2.25 bits. For 100 characters: 225 bits.

Answer: 225

questions.text:
Consider the recurrence function
[latex]T(n)=\left\{\begin{matrix} 2T(\sqrt{n})+1, & n \gt 2\\ 2,& 0 \lt n\leq 2 \end{matrix}\right.[/latex]
Then T(n) in terms of [latex]\theta[/latex] notation is
questions.solution:
Let [latex]n=2^m[/latex], [latex]S(m)=T(2^m)[/latex]: [latex]S(m)=2S(m/2)+1\Rightarrow S(m)=\Theta(m)[/latex].

[latex]T(n)=\Theta(\log n)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\theta(\log n)[/latex]
